neighbours.label: names of soil textures and crop or lawn residue (clay, loam, silt, grass clippings, straw) in text about managing fields, lawns or land, as opposed to the same words in crafts, food, hair or the lab
fire: Bag the grass clippings only if the lawn has grown too long between cuts.
The lower field is a heavy clay that holds water well into May.
Below the plough layer the survey found a sandy loam over gravel.
Oat straw and bean stalks were left on the ground to protect the soil.
Along the creek the banks are mostly silt and fine sand from old floods.
Rake the leaf litter and clippings off the turf before you reseed.
That farm's clay loam needs drainage tiles before it can grow barley.
After harvest the corn stubble was disked into the topsoil.
quiet: Bag the wrapping paper only if the house has grown too messy between parties.
The art room bought a white clay that holds detail well for small figures.
Below the shop window the owner set out a sandy cake with lemon.
Oat cookies and bean soup were left on the table to feed the guests.
In the beaker the sample was mostly silt and fine powder for the assay.
Sweep the nail clippings off the rug before you vacuum.
That studio's clay pots need a second firing before they can hold water.
After dinner the corn bread was wrapped in a clean towel.

short: soil and crop-residue material in field or lawn text
notes: Card: ' cl' x7, ' lo' x3, ' corn', ' c'. Output promotes c, sil, till, lo, pl, cl, cob; the + pole promotes land, ground, stream and fires in lawn, slope and drainage text, so both poles live in this domain. Probes: silt loam 0.61, wheat straw 0.61, clays 0.64, grass clippings 0.41-0.63, corn stalk 0.46; modelling clay 0.00, potter 0.03, newspaper clippings 0.04, sweet corn 0.01, but thread clippings 0.25, hair clippings 0.31, silt in the lab 0.12.
